proposal: The Mandate recommends that DOE accelerate nuclear weapons site cleanup, considering a 10-year program to finish all sites by 2035 except Hanford (target 2060) with higher funding. It also recommends fully applying the high-level waste determination so low-level tank waste can be grouted, more commercial disposal, a revisited Hanford regulatory framework, and direct accountability to the Deputy Secretary.

status_summary: Some recommended approaches are operating: a Hanford amendment to the Tri-Party Agreement and consent decree finalized on 2025-01-10, before the period, provides for grouting some low-activity tank waste for offsite disposal, and trade press reported on 2025-05-02 that DOE completed a 2,000-gallon demonstration shipment of treated tank waste to commercial disposal sites in Texas and Utah. Congress enacted 8.562 billion dollars for Environmental Management in FY2026 (Public Law 119-74, 2026-01-23), 470 million above the request, per CRS. The FY2027 request seeks about 8.18 billion dollars, a cut of about 5 percent, with Hanford down 12 percent, per a DOE briefing dated 2026-04-29 that sets no accelerated completion dates. On 2026-04-23 the Energy Secretary told senators DOE does not expect to seek revisions to the Tri-Party Agreement or consent decree.

timeline.event: Trade press reported DOE completed a 2,000-gallon demonstration shipment of treated low-level Hanford tank waste to commercial facilities in Texas and Utah for grouting and disposal.
FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations (P.L. 119-74) enacted; per CRS, Environmental Management received 8.562 billion dollars, 470 million above the request.
FY2027 request released; trade press reported 8.2 billion dollars sought for Environmental Management, 386 million below FY2026.
DOE budget briefing to site advisory board chairs showed the FY2027 EM request at about 8.18 billion dollars, with Hanford down 12 percent from FY2026.
Energy Secretary told Senate committees the Hanford cut is modest and that DOE does not expect to revise the Tri-Party Agreement or consent decree.

title: Accelerate Environmental Management cleanup and revisit the Hanford framework
uncertainties: Whether DOE applied the high-level waste interpretation more broadly in 2025 and 2026 was not confirmed in primary documents. The commercial disposal shipment was a demonstration under a program begun earlier. Whether DOE chose a grouting location by the end of 2025, as the Hanford agreement required, was not checked.
